title: Atlas Observation
description: One thing that was read, with its provenance. A field that could not be verified carries the literal string "unknown"; it is never filled with a plausible default, because P0.2 verifies claims against exactly these fields.

source_id.description: Stable id for this source within this snapshot, derived from snapshot_id, source_type and path. Identifies the source, not the content version: re-reading a changed file keeps the same source_id.

path.description: Relative to the snapshot root, or an identifier for a source that is not a file (a ci run is "ci://provider/workflow@ref"). Absolute forms and a ".." component are refused at construction, in both POSIX and Windows spelling: an observation is a provenance claim, and one naming a file outside the snapshot cannot be recorded.

content_sha256.description: Digest of the full content read, not of the excerpt. Authoritative identity of the bytes, independent of whether any provenance field is known. "unknown" means the observation can be cited but never confirmed.

excerpt.description: The bounded slice kept for review. Hashing covers the full content, so trimming or later redaction of this field cannot change what verification compares.

line_start.description: 1-based first line of the excerpt; 0 when the excerpt is empty.

line_end.description: 1-based last line of the excerpt; 0 when the excerpt is empty.

snapshot_id.description: Identity of the read session this observation belongs to.

ref.description: Branch or ref. Never defaulted to "main" when unverified.

commit.description: What was committed. Does NOT identify the bytes read unless worktree_state is "clean" — a dirty worktree serves different bytes from the same path.

worktree_state.description: Whether the worktree had uncommitted changes at read time.

confidentiality.description: Derived from the content at collection time when the caller states nothing: "secret" for a credential shape, "internal" for personal data, "unknown" otherwise. Never assigned "public" automatically — detection is narrow, so no match is a statement about the patterns rather than about the source. A caller that states a class is not overruled.

total_lines.description: How many lines the source has, or null when nobody counted. Null is the honest value rather than a plausible number: a count that was never taken must not let a reader conclude the excerpt is the whole file. When it is known, `line_end` may not exceed it.

read_in_full.description: Whether the excerpt is the whole source. Derived from `line_start`, `line_end` and `total_lines` rather than stored, so it cannot contradict the range it describes; null when `total_lines` is null. **Both ends count**: an excerpt that reaches the last line but starts at line 90 is not the file. An empty source, whose range is 0-0, is read in full. False is the case that matters for a `source_lacks_literal` verdict: the claim is settled about the lines it names and about nothing beyond them.
